We had an awesome time overall with the Luxury Escapes all inclusive deal at Merusaka and will be back.

My wife Terrie and I would like to especially mention the awesome staff which we engaged with daily.  In particular a special call out to Nia, LaLu, Dwi, Anjan, Injani, Bagas and Emilia who met us every time with huge smiles and welcome, as did all the staff but these individuals deserve specific recognition and hopefully rewarded.

We would also like to make a suggestion as a continuous improvement opportunity as we heard similar comments from other guests we interacted with.  This is more around efficiencies and speed of service, not staff specific.  As the bars are busy locations it seemed that there was only 1 person mixing drinks on most occasions which created quite a long wait for the service staff to deliver.  I wouldn't think it would be a cost issue given the local remuneration rates vs prices, but uplift in this efficiency would increase guest satisfaction.  This was similar in some of the restaurants also specific to drinks in the main.

These comments are not a negative only an observation from us who travel locally and internationally extensively and are involved in hospitality.

Thanks again for our wonderful holiday experience and we look forward to returning.

Andy & Terrie

Our overall experience was very positive, and what truly made our stay was the wonderful staff. In particular, Sudaria Arsa from the Indonesian restaurant went above and beyond to ensure we felt welcomed and well looked after.
There are, however, a few areas where I believe improvements could be made:
1.	The loud music at the lower poolside bar can be quite overbearing, particularly for guests who are looking to relax.
2.	The repetition of the same music track in the main upstairs dining areas (where the buffet breakfast is served) becomes quite noticeable and, at times, frustrating.
3.	Providing guests with a map of the local area would be very helpful and enhance the overall guest experience.
4.	The tour desk staff could benefit from offering broader suggestions and a wider range of options. At times, the assistance provided felt limited, and it would be helpful to recognise that one size does not fit all when catering to guests’ needs.
5.	Both the upstairs and downstairs dining areas would benefit from improved air movement. The addition of wall fans, in particular, would greatly enhance guest comfort, especially while dining.
6.	It would be beneficial to offer a shuttle service to a wider range of local destinations, such as nearby markets, rather than limiting transport options primarily to Bali Collection.
7.	Providing clearer guidance or advice on how local taxi services operate would also be helpful for guests, particularly those unfamiliar with the area.

When we first arrived the room we got smelled very musty and mouldy. 3103. We were moved to 3133 after one day and it was better but still had an odour. We found if we ran the temperature control on dry rather than cool the room was not as damp and still stayed cool.  Maybe this should be the practice when no guest is staying in the room. 
We also had a squirrel in the room at night which ran into the lights along the drapes. I believe he was getting in at the side of the building through a visible hole. 
Towels need to be undated. They are very grey with many threads. Don’t get me wrong, it was a great stay for the price. 
The location is fabulous.

Your staff are wonderful.

I was like????? I answered I want to go to the lobby and he answered are you staying at this hotel like???? Dude, hahahah even the foreigner in front of me wasn’t treated like that and they were also using a motorcycle. I answered “ofc, I stayed there and want to get my luggage”. I was so annoyed.

And at that time, I was about to get off the motorcycle and the security already asked my friend to go when I was still taking off my helmet! And my friend was about to go to the parking lot! Astaghfirullah. I stared directly at him and he said, “bisa dipercepat karna ada mobil mengantri di belakang”. Then I answered “SABAR” hahaha, and he looked at me after that. For the resort management I would have a suggestion and a request:
The suggestion is to consider an elegant way to spend time after the restaurants close!
A bar or a club located in a well-soundproof location that does not disturb other tourists would make the night party much more interesting, especially for Western tourists!
The (big) request is to approach a much more pro-active policy for keeping the beach and ocean water clean!
Perhaps a more technological solution than sending people with rakes and shovels should be addressed. Plastic pollution in the world's oceans is a problem for all of us and we should all get involved in reducing it to zero but that can only be done with concern, involvement and investment.
It's a piece of paradise there so any effort to keep it clean is worth it!

A few necessary improvements are:
*The safe needs to be removed from the floor and placed on a shelf 
(perhaps in the wardrobe). For older people like my husband and myself with back issues, it is difficult to bend down to open and close it. 
* The lack of storage space, such as drawers/shelving, means that you cannot unpack your clothes, and you need to live out of your suitcase for the duration of your stay. Also, there is only enough shelving to place one suitcase, and the other person’s suitcase has to remain on the floor and be accessed from there. 
* The kettle can only be plugged in at a PowerPoint on the floor and used down there, which is quite dangerous.
*Poor lighting in the bathroom. 
This sounds like a very long list of criticisms, but given that the resort is not new, it is, however, extremely comfortable and we would definitely stay there again. The food and beverages are very good, and the staff is excellent.

Have WhatsApp reach out to people BEFORE their stay to expedite the check-in process and give a heads up for when room is ready. Create an area specifically for people to wait with snacks/ food/ etc if you’re going to make them wait this long… among other things…
Better bathroom lighting. The orange light in the middle of the bathroom cabinet was annoying.

column49:
The staff seemed to work as a team, so no one person was responsible for each job, so it seemed they often thought “someone else will do it”.

We had a club suite with all inclusive. This was very confusing for many staff as they did not know what was included and would say we weren’t eligible for certain things that we were. Not all staff were like this, only some hassled us. We had to explain often what we were eligible for. More training is required, as it is not relaxing or hospitable having to explain yourself over and over. 

Cleaning of the floors around the facilities was not good. Old limes, cigarette butts, tissues, etc lying on the ground for 1-2 days, staff just walking past it.

On arrival, no welcome drink or cold towel was offered.

On our anniversary there was a concerning incident re the decorations in our room (see WhatsApp messages with our butler).

The butlers offered different services depending on the day. Some brought us drinks to the pool, some refused after going back and forth for an hour. It was confusing and not relaxing.

I come to Bali most years and have never seen so many staff on their phones. They would look up at the last minute and say “hello madam how may I  assist you?”, but it often felt like we were interrupting their scrolling.

The air con turned itself up every time we left the room so it was freezing on our return.  We come to Bali for a warm holiday and why do this to the environment?

We were only greeted twice in 10 nights at breakfast. We had club access so were entitled to a special menu, this was only offered twice. We had to go and find staff every other time for the menu, and many didn’t know what we talking about. We also had to find staff ourselves to take our drinks order. And why is the club breakfast so much worse than the Gading breakfast, you pay more money and get less. Also, often the tables were not set at 7am and the breakfast items were still covered with plastic or not out at all.

The shade and seating around the pool is not adequate. We put our towels down early so got good spots each day, but we felt for those who wanted a sleep in and missed out on shade or partial-shade. More sunbeds and umbrellas are needed.

The hotel itself is absolutely stunning and we enjoyed ourselves. But it could have been so much better with some extra tweaks. Staff training and attitude seem to be the things letting the hotel down.
